# Support-text classifiers

Labels: 1,000 tweets labelled by an **LLM (Claude)** following `docs/labelling_guide.md` (D-020); 200 of them were
also labelled by hand, to measure the LLM labels' quality. **Out-of-time split:** 700 October tweets
train, 300 tweets from November onwards test (the iPhone X launch falls in the test period).

## 1. Label quality: human vs LLM

| label      |   tweets |   agreement |   cohen_kappa | strength    |
|:-----------|---------:|------------:|--------------:|:------------|
| theme_code |      200 |       0.680 |         0.650 | substantial |
| sentiment  |      200 |       0.770 |         0.504 | moderate    |
| urgency    |      200 |       0.870 |         0.650 | substantial |

Kappa strength uses the Landis and Koch bands. Where the LLM labels lean, as shares of the 200 tweets: human neutral but LLM negative 18.0%, the reverse 5.0%; human urgent but LLM normal 9.5%, the reverse 3.5%. The LLM labels are more negative and less often urgent than the human's. Classifiers trained on them inherit that lean, so quote the scores against the hand labels (section 2).

## 3. Sentiment

| model                                                          |   macro_f1 |   accuracy |   neg_recall |

Where the off-the-shelf model disagrees with the labels (test period), by label and prediction:

| sentiment   | pred_sent_ots   |   tweets |
|:------------|:----------------|---------:|
| neg         | neu             |       17 |
| neg         | pos             |        8 |
| neu         | neg             |       35 |
| neu         | pos             |        3 |
| pos         | neu             |        1 |

Why it disagrees: each disagreement was read and categorised (`data/labels/sentiment_failure_review.csv`):

| category                                          |   tweets |
|:--------------------------------------------------|---------:|
| factual problem report read as negative           |       33 |
| understated or implicit complaint read as neutral |       13 |
| sarcasm read as positive                          |        7 |
| telecom jargon or product names                   |        4 |
| mixed feelings                                    |        2 |
| politeness read as positive                       |        2 |
| template or truncated text                        |        2 |
| label ambiguous                                   |        1 |

| mixed feelings                                    | pos         | neu             | . & Thx goodness 4 ur dedicated techs that work on Sunday’s. His visit today was 2 correct poorly trained or sadly misin |

| telecom jargon or product names                   | neg         | neu             | Sometimes I feel like I know more about plans and upgrade offers than 611,,.                                             |
| template or truncated text                        | neg         | pos             | Check out my result! How fast is your internet? 3Mbps when it should be 80                                               |
| mixed feelings                                    | neu         | neg             | I missed the Pixel Promo because took longer than expected to ship my phone :( loving my pixel tho.                      |

The largest group is a definitional difference, not an error: the model scores outage vocabulary ("down", "not working",
"no service") as negative, while the labelling guide calls a factual problem report neutral and leaves the problem to
the theme. Sarcasm is the clearest true failure: complaints phrased as praise ("Good job guys! Thank you!" for a
cancelled pre-order) are scored positive.
